newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-Atlantic spot power extends gains on cold.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-Atlantic spot power extends gains on cold.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Mid-Atlantic region extended their gains Monday, led by below-normal temperatures in the Northeast and stronger natural gas prices.

Temperatures in the Mid-Atlantic region are expected to slowly moderate by Wednesday but remain below-normal. Another cold front, carrying precipitation is forecast to arrive Thursday, National Weather Service reported.

Power prices in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect power pool, excluding transmission costs, for firm, peak delivery on Tuesday were quoted mostly in the $34.00-$35.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, with deals reported done in a wider range of $31.00-38.00.
These prices compare with Friday's trading range of $31.00-$32.00.
Firm, off-peak PJM electricity for Tuesday delivery climbed into the $16.00-$17.00 range from Friday's $15.00-$16.00 trading range.
Hourly PJM prices were quoted sporadically as high as $81.00 per MWh in early trading.
With temperatures expected to moderate by midweek, Tuesday through Friday firm, peak deliveries were quoted at a discount to the next-day market around $33.50.
For the remainder of January, firm, peak power prices edged into the $31.00-32.00 area, up from Friday's $30.00-$31.00 range.
February PJM power prices were also slightly higher in the $29.40-30.00 range, as compared with $29.30-$29.70 on Friday.
March PJM electricity held fairly steady in the $24.75-$25.10 range.

PJM electricity prices for April and May were up about 20 cents to the $22.50-$22.75, while June prices were talked in the $25.10-25.35 range. July/August PJM power was fairly steady at $31.30-$31.75.
Spot natural gas prices at the Philadelphia city-gate for Tuesday delivery gained about 40-50 cents to the $4.65-4.80 per million British thermal units range, traders said.
